body: [A5] Authoritative composition engine: EAP + profiles + OS/arch + license/entitlement -> runtime composition. IP-leakage guard.

brief.why: Deterministic, safe runtime composition per edition without leaking protected source.
brief.problem: Runtime composition (which components run per edition/OS/arch/entitlement) needs one authoritative engine with an IP-leakage guard.
brief.what_adds: A5 — Runtime Dependency Compiler: composes EAP + profiles + OS/arch + license/entitlement into the runtime package, with an IP-leakage guard.
brief.who_feels: PF platform maintainers, workers, and customers.

label: PF Backlog 430
title: A5: Runtime Dependency Compiler

impact_review.recommendation: Extend packaging router with /api/v1/packaging/rdc/compose and /api/v1/packaging/rdc/validate endpoints.
Enforce 5 detailed criteria (each >= 40 chars) covering multi-target OS/arch resolution, IP-leakage guard, native Go seam, fixture generation, and test coverage.
Core composition engine and IP guard implemented in native Go (go/pfcore/rdc.go); thin Python interface in core/rdc.py using core.go_host.

assumptions: Supported OS/architectures for v1: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, windows/amd64, darwin/arm64.
Customer editions (enterprise, on-prem, saas, oem) enforce strict absence of raw .py source; community/dev may allow raw .py when explicitly configured.
divergences: None: Extends canonical A1/A3/A4 pipeline without creating duplicate engines.
existing_path: go/pfcore/pfcore.go:305: native Go host library and wire request dispatcher.
config/eap-registry.json: known EAP versions and compatibility.
open_questions: None: Requirements and contracts are grounded in target architecture specs.
prior_decisions: ADR-0001 / BI-PF-0388: Shipped editions use compiled artifacts; never raw .py; one source many editions.
BI-PF-0387: Single-source delivery baseline; new shipped/sensitive logic lands in native Go.
BI-PF-0393: A1 Canonical Contracts (thin) & Go<->Python wire contract (core.contracts, go/pfcore).
BI-PF-0397: A4 EAP (Edition/Artifact Package) authoritative delivery/build manifest.
BI-PF-0398: A3 compiled packaging pipeline + NO-RAW-.py release gate.

context_review.reason: core/context_engine.py and core/agent_runtime.py already perform context composition and runtime wiring; the compiler is a natural extension. The missing items are specification decisions around license input format, target platforms, and guard placement—not architectural blockers. Blocked on BI-PF-0397 (EAP schema) and BI-PF-0398 (build pipeline) for upstream inputs.
missing: Runtime composition output format consumed by agent_runtime.py
Composition precedence rules for conflicting inputs

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/agent_hierarchy.py, core/agent_runtime.py, core/architecture_diagram.py, core/context_engine.py

approach: Compose the runtime package from EAP + profiles + OS/arch + license/entitlement; refuse compositions that would leak source.

objective: A5 — Runtime Dependency Compiler: composes EAP + profiles + OS/arch + license/entitlement into the runtime package, with an IP-leakage guard.

api_impact.reason: Exposes RDC composition and IP validation endpoints for build and packaging workflows

Build pipeline producing compiled artifacts with plug/unplug flags
Common validation engine available for reuse

language_rule: aligned: native Go in go/pfcore/rdc.go with Python seam client

MAJOR: The design states "deterministic runtime package composition" (AC1) but lacks detail on how determinism is ensured and verified, impacting integrity and reproducibility.
The "canonical A1 wire seam" and "full parity" (AC3) are not defined, nor is the strategy for ensuring parity, impacting API integrity and adaptability.
Risks are "Not specified," which is a critical omission for enterprise planning, mitigation, and long-term system health.
The design does not address availability, single-point-of-failure, or defense-in-depth (Guardrail 2), impacting system robustness.
Authorization, privilege boundaries, and tenant isolation for the RDC service are not discussed (Guardrail 3, 9; CL-011, CL-013), posing significant security and data integrity risks.
Observability (metrics, logging, alerting, ownership) is not addressed (Guardrail 10; CL-014), hindering operational maintainability and reliability.
The rollback plan "Revert the change" is generic and lacks sufficient detail for a critical component, impacting operational robustness.
MINOR: The design does not explicitly define the blast radius or include a dry-run mode for composition operations (Guardrail 4), which could impact resource utilization.
BLOCKER: The design does not define the "A1 ComponentManifest and SBOM contracts" (AC4) or detail their verification, posing a critical integrity and supply chain security risk.
The definition of "unprotected raw .py source files" (AC2) is missing, making the core IP-leakage guard mechanism ambiguous and potentially ineffective.
The "fail-closed" mechanism for the IP-leakage guard (AC2) is not detailed or proven, which is a critical security vulnerability.
The design does not attach current-run red proof for the real runtime entrypoint (CL-010), failing a mandatory design guardrail.
The role of `core/rdc.py` is unclear; if new core logic is added here, it violates the "new shipped logic -> Go" language standard.

MINOR: The `core/packaging.py` module introduces redundant wrapper functions (`rdc_compose`, `rdc_validate_ip`) that simply call `core.rdc` functions, adding an unnecessary layer of indirection.
The `generated_at` timestamp in `sample-runtime-package/runtime-composition.json` is hardcoded, which is inconsistent with a dynamically generated field.

NIT: The `ip_zone` field is hardcoded to "A" in both `ValidateIPLeakage` and `Compose` functions in `go/pfcore/rdc.go`, which might limit future flexibility if multiple IP zones are introduced.

The `scripts/dev/deliver.py` changes introduce a new `create_pr` argument and associated logic, which is a significant addition to a core delivery script and could benefit from its own dedicated test suite.
MINOR: The `write_runtime_package` function in `core/rdc.py` only materializes mock binary artifacts when `dry_run` is true; for a non-dry-run, it only writes the manifest, which is inconsistent with its name implying full package assembly.

NIT: In `go/pfcore/rdc.go`, `ValidateIPLeakage` includes redundant checks `!strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".pyc") && !strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".pyd")` alongside `strings.HasSuffix(lower, ".py")`, since filenames ending in `.pyc` or `.pyd` already fail the `.py` suffix check.
MINOR: The OpenAPI specification (`product-forge/api/openapi.json`) omits the 400 response contract for `/api/v1/packaging/rdc/compose` and `/api/v1/packaging/rdc/validate`, despite the router raising `ApiError("VALIDATION_FAILED")` on validation/IP-leakage failure.
SUMMARY: Implementation successfully fulfills all acceptance criteria for BI-PF-0399.
Native Go runtime dependency compiler engine and fail-closed IP guard adhere strictly to language and contract boundaries.
Pipeline tests cover hermetic resolution, target filtering, and REST API exposure cleanly.

acceptance_criteria: The Runtime Dependency Compiler (RDC) accepts an EAP manifest, target OS/arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64, windows/amd64, darwin/arm64), and license profile to produce a deterministic runtime package composition.
The IP-leakage guard fail-closed rejects any composition for customer/commercial editions (enterprise, saas, on-prem, oem) that contains unprotected raw .py source files.
The native Go engine in go/pfcore exposes rdc.compose and rdc.validate_ip ops over the canonical A1 wire seam with full parity.
The sample-runtime-package/ fixture and manifest are generated and verified against the A1 ComponentManifest and SBOM contracts.
A comprehensive automated test suite in test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_a5_rdc.py verifies hermetic resolution, multi-target OS/arch filtering, and IP-leakage prevention.

sig:2dd824c8e4161bd8.note: OpenAPI 400 response contract for rdc endpoints: Router returns standard ApiError 400 mapped globally in FastAPI exception handlers; 200 payload reflects status/error contract.

sig:237e627b8ff104ae.note: Redundant suffix check in ValidateIPLeakage: Defensive coding ensures clarity that compiled extensions (.pyc, .pyd) are explicitly permitted while source (.py) is rejected.

sig:0408d3548dd385ab.note: Robustness addressed via stateless in-memory compilation and fail-closed error handling in go/pfcore/rdc.go.

sig:05b53633233ace83.note: Defined unprotected raw .py source files strictly as any readable UTF-8/ASCII .py source text file not compiled into binary (.so/.pyd) in go/pfcore/rdc.go:ValidateIPLeakage.

sig:08f9d3221ec67888.note: Explicit risks and concrete mitigations for IP exposure and cross-compilation target resolution are recorded in engineering/design/BI-PF-0399.md.

sig:239f18aba4477f22.note: core/rdc.py is strictly a thin client invoking native Go logic via core.go_host.invoke, adhering to the language rule with core logic in go/pfcore/rdc.go.

sig:292a0f7f1c9a1f59.note: Attached proof in test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_a5_rdc.py executing the real entrypoint core/rdc.py:compose_runtime_package.

sig:3f0aa1faee4518ff.note: A1 ComponentManifest and SBOM contracts are validated against core/contracts.py schemas in test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_a5_rdc.py and go/pfcore/rdc_test.go.

sig:793fe6755772cc04.note: Authorization enforced via PF_API_TOKEN with operator/platform_admin role boundary in api/routers/packaging.py.

sig:90d8c269dfb0c105.note: Canonical A1 wire seam uses WireRequest/WireResponse schemas in core/contracts.py and go/pfcore/pfcore.go with matching tests in go/pfcore/rdc_test.go.

sig:a28517f51402f85c.note: Dry-run mode supported via dry_run flag in rdc.compose in go/pfcore/rdc.go and core/rdc.py.

sig:ab855033a2c86970.note: The IP-leakage guard in go/pfcore/rdc.go is fail-closed: customer editions (enterprise, on-prem, saas, oem) immediately abort packaging with ERR_RDC_IP_LEAKAGE if any .py is found.

sig:dde75d6b0667abfd.note: Detailed rollback plan: revert PR merge commit with zero database schema migrations in engineering/design/BI-PF-0399.md.

sig:e1603be655440fc4.note: Determinism is guaranteed by sorting component lists, normalizing forward-slash relative paths, and hashing all artifacts with SHA-256 in go/pfcore/rdc.go.

sig:ec3f6f362035857c.note: Observability logs structured JSON events for composition milestones and IP guard verdicts in core/rdc.py and api/routers/packaging.py.
